trickyParts: nats-server 2.10.29 reports ack floor 0 for a fresh consumer, so every session consumer is created at a start sequence (stream last+1) and the floor is read never below it

nats-server 2.10 handles one connection's JetStream API requests one at a time; a 1,000-session restart was bounded by that until the listener read all consumers in one paged CONSUMER.LIST and started pulls without a consumer info

A restart that deleted a consumer and failed its create lost the position; the pending start is now recorded before the delete and used by whichever call creates the consumer next (in-process only; a second listener does not know it)
The Claude Code bridge answers an inbox delivery only on Claude Code's isReplay echo of that user message; the live test's flag check had to follow main moving the argv into claudelaunch.go
deviations: Plan's replay-without-polling is proven on the consumer path; the core path keeps #2228's /v1/replay catch-up as the fallback (planned departure 1)

Load: Dispatch commits only about 0.5-0.6 events/s of the 40/s offered on the 2-core pod, so delivery latency rests on about 1,900-2,300 receipts per run plus a labelled supplement that publishes Dispatch-shaped events straight to NATS at 40/s
nats-server RSS grows over a 10-minute window on both sides (before and after); not caused by this change, and a 10-minute window cannot show whether it levels off

No real-stack test covers the core path's recovery after a frozen NATS path any more: the shared stall scenario (INFRA-548) now checks consumer delivery, since the stack's listener answers consumer; mocked unit tests in both plugins still cover the core path
The listener grant change (session-consumer entries, CONSUMER.LIST, envoy-roles) reaches a hub only at its next replacement or reload; until then the listener answers core and the old path runs
